Lesson · 25 min

Spreadsheet Basics: Entering and Formatting Data

Learn the Sheets screen, enter and edit data, format cells and numbers, freeze the header row, and work with sheet tabs.

By the end of this lesson you can

  • ✓Name the parts of the Sheets screen: cells, rows, columns, the name box, the formula bar, and sheet tabs
  • ✓Enter, edit, and clear data, and move between cells with Enter and Tab
  • ✓Format cells: bold, fill color, borders, and number formats such as currency and dates
  • ✓Freeze the header row, and add and rename sheets

Lesson Notes

Read through the key concepts before you try the challenge.

The Sheets screen

On the job

You keep Parkview's rent roll.

Priya, the bookkeeper, keeps the rent roll for Elm Street Apartments in a Google Sheet. It is hard to read: the headers look like the data, the rents have no dollar signs, and the header row scrolls away when you look at the bottom of the list. A new tenant also needs to be added.

Your task: Add the new tenant and format the sheet so anyone can read it.

  • Click a cell and type. Press Enter to save the entry and move down, or Tab to move right.
  • To change a cell, click it and type over it, or double-click it (or press F2) to edit part of it.
  • To clear cells, select them and press Delete.
  • Like Docs, Sheets saves every change to Drive. There is no Save button.

Formatting cells and numbers

  • Select the cells first: click and drag, or click a column letter or row number to select the whole column or row.
  • Bold, text color, Fill color, Borders, and Merge cells are on the toolbar.
  • Number formats: Format as currency ($) and Format as percent (%) are on the toolbar. More formats (123) and Format › Number list the rest: Number, Date, Time, Accounting, and more.
  • Shortcuts: Ctrl+Shift+4 currency, Ctrl+Shift+5 percent, Ctrl+Shift+1 number with decimals.
  • Decrease or increase decimal places with the .0 and .00 buttons.
  • Widen a column: drag the line at the right edge of its letter, or double-click that line to fit the longest entry.
A number format changes how a number looks, not the number. 1450 formatted as currency shows $1,450.00, and formulas still use 1450.

Freeze rows and work with sheets

  • View › Freeze › 1 row keeps the header row on screen while you scroll. Choose No rows to unfreeze.
  • Add a sheet with + at the bottom left (or Shift+F11). Double-click a sheet tab to rename it.
  • Right-click a tab to duplicate, delete, color, hide, or protect a sheet.
Worked example

Making the rent roll readable

Turn a plain list into a rent roll anyone can read.

  1. 1

    Bold the header row and give it a light fill color.

    Readers instantly tell the labels from the data.

  2. 2

    Format the rent column as currency.

    Dollar signs and two decimals show it is money.

  3. 3

    View › Freeze › 1 row.

    The labels stay visible at the bottom of a long list.

  4. 4

    Rename the tab Elm Street.

    When Riverside gets its own tab, everyone knows which is which.

Result: A rent roll that is easy to scan and hard to misread.

🔑 Format the header, the numbers, and the tabs before you share a sheet.

Challenge

Apply what you've learned in this lesson.

Build a small list in your own Google account.

  1. Create a spreadsheet named Budget Practice. In row 1, type Item, Category, Cost, and Date.
  2. Enter at least five rows of practice expenses (use Tab to move right and Enter to move down).
  3. Bold the header row and give it a fill color. Format the Cost column as currency and the Date column as a date.
  4. Freeze the header row. Rename the sheet tab Expenses.
Deliverable: Share the spreadsheet with your instructor as a Viewer, or submit a screenshot, to your instructor or course folder. No Google account? Complete the practice simulation and submit its results page.
